$comment: The renames this package has made, as DATA. Three things read this file, which is
the point — the hub declares a rename once and everything else follows:
1. build.js       emits a deprecated alias for every `token` entry, so spoke source
keeps resolving the moment the rename lands.
2. migrate-tokens.mjs  rewrites a spoke's source from `from` to `to`.
3. doctor.mjs     warns a spoke that it is still on deprecated names.
WHY THIS EXISTS: spokes consume this package through a `file:` symlink, so a rename
here reaches every spoke on their next dev tick — there is no publish step to absorb
it, and a bare `var(--old-name)` does not fall back, it drops the whole declaration.
A rename used to be tribal knowledge in one person's head. Now it is a row here.
ADDING A RENAME: add the entry in the same commit as the rename. If you rename
without adding a row, the alias is not emitted and spokes break silently.

migrations.why: `type` is a homonym (typography? or a variable's type?). Tier-1 typography converged on `--<css-property>-<value>`, and the property is font-size.
The only sub-100 step in the system written without padding, so shadows sorted wrong in every alphabetical listing.

The composite `--shadow-050…500` were ordinal names for intents living in tier 1 — the same misfiling that put `--transition-fast` there. Tier 1 now holds only the raw axes (offset-x / offset-y / blur / spread / color); clustering them into a usable box-shadow is the semantic act, so the composites are `--elevation-1…6` at tier 2. The old names also formed a 1:1 passthrough — six primitives, six roles, no reuse — so nothing was lost by collapsing them. A spoke should read the tier-2 role, which is the one it is allowed to override. NOTE: `--shadow-50` (the earlier `shadow-50-padding` row) still points at `--shadow-050` and resolves through this row's alias — custom-property resolution is order-independent, so the two-hop chain holds.

`--color-status-*` were tier-1 ALIASES of ramp steps. The tier-2 roles already existed and merely detoured through them, so the detour was deleted. A spoke reading the tier-1 name should read the tier-2 role instead — that is the one it is allowed to override.
An alias of --font-sans that nothing read. Deleted rather than moved.

A composite class now carries the same name as the tokens it assembles: .typography-body-sm reads --typography-body-sm-*. The old names described the PLACE (page-title, card-title) rather than the intention plus a size.

The ONE rename in this file that changes rendering. `.type-code` was font-size-100; code now tracks body, whose smallest step is font-size-150, so there is no exact equivalent. Mapped to the nearest step rather than to -md, which would jump two. Inline code gets slightly larger.

Tier-2 colour used two opposite word orders: property-first for neutrals (text-primary, border-light) and intention-first for everything else (danger-border, primary-strong), so no name was predictable. Now every token is <property>-<intention>-<variant>-<state>, property being background | content | border. `primary` became `brand` because it meant two different things — the brand hue AND the most-prominent text. `-strong` became `content-*`: those tokens were step 11, TEXT on a surface, but read like a bolder fill and got used as one. Two pairs originally collapsed into a sibling (primary-active into brand-hover, text-tertiary into content-secondary) because the hub's values were identical; that was reverted — identical defaults do not make a themeable token redundant, and a spoke had already separated both.

The translucent washes now lead with `overlay`, matching the property-first order of the rest of tier-2 colour. `overlay` is a deliberate fourth property: these sit OVER a background rather than being one, and naming them background-* would collide with the opaque neutrals that already own those names.

UI text runs at three sizes and two weights in the component kit; `label` shipped with one of each, which is why 59 rules across 54 components set typography by hand instead of naming a role. `label` is now `label-xs` alongside `label-sm`/`label-md` and a `-strong` weight variant, following the same shape `body-*` and `code-*` already use.
The caps treatment exists at two sizes — the page-level eyebrow and the menu group heading one step up. Same intention, so one role with a size variant rather than two roles.
Class names track their tokens: .typography-label-xs reads --typography-label-xs-*.

A size-only ramp running parallel to the typography composites. It let a component pick a size without adopting a composite, which is how the kit ended up with 100 tier-1 font-size reads and no shared typographic vocabulary. Its nine tier-3 consumers now point at the composite whose job matches — form control text at label, the large step at body-lg — so the size travels with a weight, a line-height and a face instead of alone.

The word `border` named two different things at tier 3. These two held a plain colour; --filter-dropdown-border held a whole `1px solid …` shorthand (see the row below, which is NOT an exact alias). All three are now `-border-color`, matching the 27 border hooks in the file that already were. Names only, values untouched. FIRST TIER-3 ROWS IN THIS FILE — note the asymmetry: the emitted alias rescues a spoke that READS an old name, but tier 3 is the surface a spoke DECLARES, and an alias cannot rescue a declaration. A spoke that overrode --sidenav-border silently loses that override and renders the hub default with no error, so /update-tokens has to run in every spoke rather than the alias being left to absorb it.

NOT an exact alias — the VALUE SHAPE changed, not just the name. --filter-dropdown-border held `1px solid var(--color-border)`; --filter-dropdown-border-color holds the colour alone, and esa-filter-dropdown now composes the shorthand from --border-width-default. The hub renders identically (that role is 1px, the same literal the shorthand carried), but a spoke is NOT safe by construction here: anything that wrote `border: var(--filter-dropdown-border)` now gets a bare colour where a shorthand was, which is not a valid border. That is the whole reason the token changed — a theme could not re-point this colour without restating a width and style it had no reason to care about. Rewrite such a site as `border: var(--border-width-default, 1px) solid var(--filter-dropdown-border-color)`.

Five tokens put their variant AFTER the property, where the rest of the file puts it before (--app-bar-brand-bg, --app-bar-brand-strong-text). Four were esa-snackbar-item's colour-variant surface — the only component in the kit that exposes its variant axis at tier 3 at all — and the fifth, --form-border-color-error, put a validation VARIANT in the trailing slot reserved for interaction states, beside hover and focus. Renaming it also pairs it with the existing --form-error-color: one error treatment, two properties. Names only; every value is untouched. Same tier-3 declaration caveat as the border row above.
